To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the customer–supplier/ lead–lag effect is a global phenomenon and that it exhibits characteristics consistent with slow diffusion of information.
(1) The customer–supplier effect is robust to a variety of alternative specifications, including the use of a customer–supplier network that is based on the value chain of a firm.
the lead-lag effect is robust to alternative definitions of lead and lag industries, is robust across countries, and is not driven by industry-level characteristics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the predictability of returns and with the information content of returns.
the predictability of stock market returns, and we focus on the information content of customer-supplier linkages.
the question: Does the customer–supplier relationship affect the predictability of returns?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the customer–supplier relationship has no predictive power in terms of stock returns.
customer industries lead supplier industries in the diffusion of information.
there is evidence of lead-lag relationships between customer and supplier stocks, and that these relationships can be explained by a slow diffusion of information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the customer–supplier effect is not a global phenomenon.
we have shown that customer–supplier relationships are important for stock market valuation and that this relationship is stronger when the customer–supplier relationship is more concentrated.
customer industries lead supplier industries by 3–4 months in the international equity markets, and that the effect is stronger when customer industries are more sensitive to the business cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lead–lag effect is not a phenomenon that is unique to the US.
the customer–supplier/ lead–lag effect is a robust and pervasive feature of international stock markets.
customer industries lead the returns of supplier firms, but this is not the case for supplier firms leading the returns of customer firms.
